title: The 2-Minute Rule That Eliminates Procrastination
tone: Calm authority, evidence-based, relatable office moments

concept.hook: There's a 2-minute task sitting in your inbox right now that's costing you hours of anxiety.
concept.story_arc: Problem (unfinished tasks drain energy) → Rule (do it now) → Evidence (neuroscience) → Examples → Call to action

audio.narration: There's a 2-minute task sitting in your inbox right now that's costing you hours of anxiety. Most of us ignore small tasks until they become massive stressors. But what if you could stop that spiral in under 2 minutes? Here's the neuroscience. Each unfinished task consumes what scientists call cognitive RAM. Your brain is keeping that task open in the background — constantly. The more open loops you have, the less actual thinking power you have available. The rule is simple: if a task takes less than 2 minutes, do it immediately. Don't add it to your list. Reply to that quick email. File that receipt. Send that five-word Slack reply. Each one you complete frees up your working memory. Finishing a task — even a tiny one — gives your brain a dopamine hit and a sense of progress. That's the real value. Not the task itself, but the clarity it creates. Next time you see a 2-minute task, ask yourself: is this worth my anxiety for the next week? Do it now. And if you want more productivity science that actually works, subscribe.

metadata.youtube_description:
There's a 2-minute task sitting in your inbox right now that's costing you hours of anxiety. In this video, I break down the neuroscience behind why unfinished tasks drain your cognitive energy, and the simple 2-minute rule that top performers use to stay focused and clear.

📌 What you'll learn:
- Why your brain keeps unfinished tasks 'open' in the background
- The 2-minute rule and how to apply it immediately
- Real examples: quick email, filing, calendar invites
- How finishing tiny tasks creates dopamine and mental clarity

⏱️ Timestamps:
00:00 — Hook
00:10 — The problem: cognitive RAM drain
00:25 — The 2-minute rule
00:45 — Real examples
00:55 — Call to action

🔔 Subscribe for weekly productivity science.
